items.a: RSS Lingo is a mobile RSS reader that helps you learn a language. Add feeds you care about, read comfortably, and translate articles with your own AI key. Everything is stored on your device.

items.q: How do I add a feed?
items.a: Tap + Add feed and paste a direct RSS URL like https://example.org/rss.xml. The feed is fetched immediately.

items.q: Where can I find an RSS URL?
items.a: Look for an "RSS" or "Feed" link in the site footer or header. You can also try /rss.xml, /feed/, or /atom.xml. Pasting the site address alone is not supported yet — auto-discovery is planned.
Save keeps an article forever. Without saving, only the newest 50 articles per feed are kept.
Articles live in a local database on your device only.

items.q: How do I set up translation?
items.a: Open Settings (⚙), pick a provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, or Gemini), enter a model name (e.g. gpt-4o-mini, claude-sonnet-4-5, gemini-2.0-flash), paste your own API key from that provider (get it at platform.openai.com, console.anthropic.com, or aistudio.google.com), pick the target language, and tap Test connection.

items.q: Where is my API key stored?
items.a: Your key is stored in the device's secure storage (iOS Keychain / Android Keystore). It is sent only to the provider you chose, only when you translate. We have no servers and never see your key.

items.q: What languages does the app support?
items.a: The app interface follows your device language (English, Russian, or Finnish). The translation target language is set separately in Settings.
